analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3), adds a paragraph on NemotronSuperOpenRouterVideoTests (head lines ~1073-1077), and adds a paragraph on NemotronSuperOpenRouterCapabilityTests (head lines ~1097-1104). There are no source, workflow, config or permission changes, so no runtime security behavior changes.

The new text describes CPU-only tests: the video readiness clips are read through the source tree, and the capability tests replay request shapes from a platform-pinned conformance fixture. The tests exercise the inbound decode, request plan, template, parser and media decode on a tiny installed fixture. It states that no model is loaded and no answer quality is measured, so it does not overclaim runtime secrecy or correctness (T-056). Nothing relaxes the cache, attestation, authorization or encryption controls (T-041, T-053, T-054, TB-011). No credentials, production endpoints or private data are referenced.

The docs describe tests that are not in the supplied evidence. I could not verify that the referenced test suites or the SDK MiMoOpenRouter resources exist, or that they behave as described. This is a documentation accuracy question, not a security regression. The reviewed file list contains only the changed documentation file, and the base text for it was examined in full across all three units.
